text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Another step towards democratisation will be taken on Monday as Nigeria's five political parties begin congresses to choose candidates for March 15 local council polls.

- Technical partner in the Nigerian liquefied natural gas project, Royal Dutch Shell, refuting Italian media reports, says it supports legal action against Italian utility firm Enel for cancelling contract to buy Nigerian gas.

- Former interior minister retired Major-General Mohammed Magoro, four others, appear before failed bank tribunal over alleged debt of 29.78 million naira owed Oceanic Bank; case adjourned to April 22.
- Former head of state and chairman of Vision 2010 project Ernest Shonekan in a paper presented in London urges British businesses to set up new banking institutions in Nigeria.
- Uncertainty shrouds visit of U.N. rapporteurs to Nigeria as neither of the two men expected in Lagos on Sunday night turns up for the mission to investigate the judicial system.
- Investment Banking and Trust Company's equity fund, the nation's largest unit trust, was subscribed by about 75 percent or 1.5 billion naira by the close of applications in January.
- Central bank withdraws 8.365 billion naira from circulation through sale of treasury bills.
- Shareholders seek to raise capital base of trading conglomerate John Holt Plc by 150 percent or from 300 million naira to 500 million naira.

- Rodney Little, president of British-Nigeria chamber of commerce, tells seminar in London that investment climate in Nigeria is now attractive and urges British businesses to take advantage of stable policies in the last two fiscal budgets.

- Speedwing, consulting arm of British Airways, recommends that Nigerian government shuts down its troubled national carrier Nigeria Airways for six months for a necessary relaunch strategy to be put in place.
- Banks may press for phased recapitalisation following government directive that they should raise their capital base nine-fold to a minimum of 500 million naira by December 1998.
